title: I made a game with GPT 5.6
author: GlitteringJob9248
selftext:
It’s a back room simulator the prompt is to create a back room simulator, then I iterated it with several rounds, tbh I am still improving it right now. I think compare to Fable, gpt 5.6 sol needs a little more hand holding, less able to one shot games, but still very happy about the result!

Here is the game link. Null Aisle

https://www.aigameshare.com/games/null-aisle?play=1&mode=fullscreen

Trust me, it is not a horror game :)

comments.author: Nasdali
comments.body: It's a vibe for sure. It's like backrooms meet severance.  Like the look.

comments.author: Bitcoin1x
comments.body: It looks like a PlayStation 1 and a 1/2 game. Nicely done

comments.author: abulero
comments.body: Were you able to achieve everything with AI? Even the textures, models and UI elements? Or just the coding?

replies.author: GlitteringJob9248
replies.body: everything with ai, everything is calculated by code

comments.author: luminis_dev
comments.body: It’s interesting to see how AI will evolve in the game dev space for the next few years.

replies.author: knightenrichman
replies.body: The oversaturation of the market will begin soon...

replies.author: luminis_dev
replies.body:
Do you think that those who refrain from using AI generated gameplay ideas will standout ?
(Meaning they can still use AI to help them create, but not telling them to “Generate this game for me, from A - Z”)

replies.author: knightenrichman
replies.body: Unless someone makes the next Balatro, I think there's a good chance the market is going to be flooded with ai games to the point it will be really hard to get attention for your game at all without spending a lot of money on advertising.
